content.user_title: Check Japan Rainfall and Short-Term Radar Forecasts
content.value_statement: Daily plans can depend on rainfall at a specific location during the next hour. This skill guides assistants through public JMA radar data to report approximate rainfall intensity and short-term changes.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve available observation and forecast timestamps from public JMA endpoints without an API key or login.
Calculate XYZ tile coordinates from latitude, longitude, and zoom using the provided Python example.
Download radar PNG tiles for available observation or forecast times.
Inspect tile palette indices with Pillow to estimate rainfall intensity at a selected pixel.
Compare current observations with upcoming forecast tiles and report timestamps in Japan Standard Time.
Handle failed requests with limited retries, refreshed timestamp lists, and a link to the official JMA map.
limitations: The color legend is approximate and does not establish official rainfall rates in millimeters per hour.
The scope is short-term rainfall in Japan, not tomorrow's weather, warnings, earthquakes, or tsunami information.
Execution requires network access, curl, Python, and Pillow or ImageMagick; pixel coordinates must be supplied for the image example.
The referenced shared response checklist is not included in this skill package.

use_cases.title: Plan a Short Commute
use_cases.description: Compare current rainfall and available forecasts near a station before choosing when to leave.

use_cases.title: Schedule an Outdoor Visit
use_cases.description: Check approximate rainfall near a destination during the next 30 to 60 minutes.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Outdoor Work
use_cases.description: Review timestamped radar estimates near a work site and communicate uncertainty before scheduling short outdoor tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Rain
prompt_templates.prompt: Check current rainfall near latitude 35.68, longitude 139.77. Report approximate intensity and the observation time in JST.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: retrieve a current radar observation for known coordinates.

prompt_templates.title: Compare the Next Hour
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current rainfall with available forecasts over the next hour near latitude 35.68, longitude 139.77. Include JST timestamps and uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare observations with multiple forecast times.

prompt_templates.title: Check Several Locations
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare rainfall now and over the next 30 minutes at these Japan coordinates: [locations]. Separate observations from forecasts and report unavailable data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare multiple locations without treating missing data as dry weather.

prompt_templates.title: Review the Radar Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: For [latitude, longitude], report returned JMA timestamps, tile coordinates, and sampled palette indices. Compare neighboring pixels and separate estimates from verified facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: inspect the evidence supporting a local rainfall estimate.

output_examples.input: Show an illustrative rainfall report with observation and forecast times in JST.
output: Illustrative report, not live weather data.
At 14:50 JST, the observation tile indicates approximately weak rainfall near the selected location.
The 15:20 JST forecast tile suggests stronger rainfall.
Intensity is a qualitative radar estimate, not an official rainfall rate or a ground measurement.

output_examples.input: Show an example response when the timestamp endpoint remains unavailable after retries.
output: Rain-cloud data could not be retrieved after retries.
Current rainfall and the short-term outlook are unknown.
Check the official JMA weather map for available information.

best_practices: Use timestamp pairs returned by JMA and include JST times with every observation and forecast.
Describe intensity as approximate and inspect nearby pixels when a single pixel may be noisy.
Report retrieval failures explicitly and use an isolated environment when installing optional image tools.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret failed requests, missing tiles, or unavailable forecasts as evidence of no rain.
Do not invent timestamp pairs or present the measured palette as an official millimeters-per-hour legend.
Do not use this short-term radar skill as a substitute for official warnings or longer-range forecasts.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key or account?
faq.answer: No. The documented JMA endpoints provide public weather data without an API key or login.

faq.question: Which locations and forecast period does it cover?
faq.answer: It targets locations in Japan and rainfall changes over roughly the next 30 to 60 minutes, subject to available forecast tiles.

faq.question: Does it provide exact rainfall rates?
faq.answer: No. Palette colors support approximate intensity descriptions, but the skill does not verify an official color-to-millimeters-per-hour mapping.

faq.question: What tools are needed?
faq.answer: The examples use curl and Python. Pixel inspection requires Pillow or ImageMagick, and the selected pixel coordinates must be supplied.

faq.question: What happens when JMA data is unavailable?
faq.answer: The instructions allow one or two retries, then report unavailable data and direct users to the official JMA map.

faq.question: Does it handle weather warnings or tomorrow's forecast?
faq.answer: No. The author directs those questions to separate weather and disaster-alert skills, which are not included here.
